analysis.title: Around the world in 80 charts: Tracking the US import cycle
key_insights: Global air and ocean freight volume growth remains strong at around HSD% yoy on the latest readings (Exhibit 1). Drivers are Chinese manufacturing growth on the supply side, and on the demand side the positive inflection in the US inventory cycle since Q1 plus growing datacenter-related volumes.
Chinese port volumes rebounded 10-20% yoy in Sep/Oct after earlier weather-related disruptions (Exhibit 6). US West Coast import volumes jumped c.20% yoy (Exhibit 11).

The current US import surge looks set to start tapering during Nov (Exhibit 12), at growth levels consistent with prior re-stocking cycle peaks in 2024 (pre-tariffs) and 2020/21 (goods vs. services spending surge).
An earlier Chinese New Year in 2027 should keep volumes well supported seasonally into year-end.

Downside risk to Q1 2027 volume growth comes from a maturing re-stocking cycle. US inventory levels expanded at their fastest pace since Oct 2022 (Exhibit 14), earlier Chinese NY becomes a seasonal headwind, US retailers forecast lower import growth into next year (Exhibit 13), and US economists model a positive but sequentially lower capex growth impulse in 2027.

Container freight rates have been broadly stable close to historical highs in recent months (Exhibit 31). Rates into the US are close to COVID-era highs on the import volume surge (Exhibit 33), while rates into Europe (Exhibit 32) and LatAm (Exhibit 36) have declined.
On Asia-Europe, capacity is being freed by a fast return of liner services to the Suez route (Exhibit 22). This is partly offset by high port congestion (Exhibit 54).

The ocean capacity cycle is at an inflection point (low in Q4 2026). Net fleet growth is set to accelerate during 2027 before slowing again during 2029 (Exhibit 45). The orderbook is 44% of existing global capacity, mostly for delivery in the next three years (Exhibit 44).

Air cargo rates remain strong into year-end, up c.30% yoy on the latest readings (Exhibit 24). Cargo load factors are rising, which explains the move in rates (Exhibit 26). Asia outbound air cargo correlates with the semiconductor cycle (Exhibit 30).

European airlines have cut capacity, especially in short-haul. This has rebalanced supply and demand and moved nominal fare growth from flat-ish in the summer quarters to MSD-HSD% positive going into winter (Exhibits 58, 60). At spot jet fuel this still implies significant fuel-adjusted, real-terms fare declines.

Long-haul airline routes remain stronger. Asia-Europe capacity remains constrained by the Middle East situation, and North Atlantic carriers remain highly disciplined on capacity (Exhibit 65). Middle East airline schedules remain HSD% below last year's levels (Exhibit 57).

Airports show generally low growth this winter. Frankfurt seat capacity outlook remains negative, Gatwick traffic has been declining, Zurich traffic is up +4% YTD but fading into winter, and AENA winter seats are set to grow MSD% (Exhibits 72-75).
Roads: French motorway traffic trends weakened in Q3, while Eurotunnel cross-channel traffic improved in recent months (Exhibits 77, 81).

Commodity shipping: crude tanker rates strengthened on high shipping demand and constrained vessel supply. Dry bulk rates are lower in line with Chinese commodity imports. Orderbooks are rising for VLCCs and for bulkers, where new orders are c.19% of the Capesize fleet (Exhibits 82-85).

sector_views.rationale: Current trading is strong with rates near historical highs, but the outlook is weaker: the Suez return frees capacity, the orderbook is 44% of fleet, and fleet growth re-accelerates in 2027.
Capacity discipline is lifting fares from flat-ish to MSD-HSD% positive going into winter, with long-haul stronger than short-haul.
Generally low growth this winter, with divergent seat capacity outlooks across Frankfurt, Gatwick, Zurich, AENA and ADP.

earnings_insights: GS expects higher RASK growth for IAG in Q4 (Exhibit 66, which labels 3Q26 IAG PRASK as a GS estimate).

risk_factors: A maturing US re-stocking cycle and fading import growth in Q1 2027.
An earlier Chinese New Year in 2027 becomes a seasonal headwind in Q1.
US retailers forecast lower import growth into next year.
The Suez return and the ocean orderbook (44% of fleet) add capacity, with net fleet growth re-accelerating during 2027.
High port congestion persists, and FX (EUR/CNY) is a potential headwind to euro area import growth.
Dec European short-haul fares depend on late bookings.
charts_described: Exhibit 12: Port of LA imports and future schedules (4-week MA yoy) show a huge spike in imports into LA this fall, with the text expecting a taper from November.
Exhibit 14: The Logistics Managers' Index inventory expansion rate reached its highest level since Sep-22 in Oct-26.
Exhibit 44: 44% of existing global container capacity is on order, mostly for delivery in the next three years.
Exhibit 24: Air cargo rates up ~30% yoy.
geopolitical: Asia-Europe airline capacity remains constrained by the situation in the Middle East.
Liner services are returning to the Suez route, freeing up existing vessels.
Port congestion in India remains high, reflecting network changes linked to events in the Arabian Gulf.
Middle East airline schedules remain HSD% below last year's levels (a March pre-conflict comparison is shown).

tension_points.bull_case: Global air and ocean freight volumes are growing around HSD% yoy. Chinese port volumes rebounded 10-20% yoy in Sep/Oct, US West Coast imports jumped c.20% yoy, and an earlier Chinese New Year supports volumes into year-end.
tension_points.bear_case: The import surge tapers from November to levels consistent with prior re-stocking peaks. US inventories expanded at their fastest pace since Oct 2022, US retailers forecast lower import growth, and the earlier Chinese NY becomes a Q1 2027 headwind.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A taper in US import growth during November (Exhibit 12), or lower retailer import volumes around the turn of the year (Exhibit 13), would confirm the bear case.

tension_points.bull_case: Rates are broadly stable near historical highs. Asia-US rates are close to COVID-era highs on the import surge, and port congestion remains high.
tension_points.bear_case: The Suez return frees up vessels, the orderbook is 44% of the fleet, and net fleet growth re-accelerates during 2027. Rates into Europe and LatAm have already declined.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Net fleet growth re-accelerating during 2027, with the ocean capacity cycle low in Q4 2026, would undermine the bull case.
